draft.title: The definite integral
card: The definite integral of f(x) from a to b is written ∫ f(x) dx, with a at the bottom and b at the top. a and b are called the limits.
To find it, first find an antiderivative F(x). Then the value is F(b) − F(a): put in the top limit, put in the bottom limit, and subtract. This is the fundamental theorem of calculus.
The constant C is not needed. It would appear in both F(b) and F(a), so it cancels.
For the integral of 2x from 1 to 3, F(x) = x². Then F(3) − F(1) = 9 − 1 = 8.
draft.remember: Definite integral = F(top) − F(bottom), and C cancels.

a.q: What is the value of the integral of 3x² from 1 to 2?
a.why: An antiderivative of 3x² is x³. Then F(2) − F(1) = 8 − 1 = 7. The answer 8 comes from using only F(2) and forgetting to subtract F(1).
a.clue: Find F(x), then subtract the bottom value from the top.

b.q: What is the value of the integral of (4x − 1) from 0 to 3?
b.why: An antiderivative is 2x² − x. Then F(3) = 18 − 3 = 15 and F(0) = 0, so the value is 15 − 0 = 15. The answer 18 comes from forgetting to integrate the −1 term, and −15 comes from subtracting in the wrong order.
b.clue: Integrate both terms, then put in 3 and 0.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out (7 and 15), and the explanations correctly account for the distractors.
